newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan employment conditions steadily improving - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan employment conditions steadily improving - BOJ.

text.p: Japan's employment conditions are steadily improving, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) said in a report released on Friday.

The report on employment conditions said that with the recovery in private demand in Japan becoming firmer, firms were gradually ridding themselves of a feeling that they had too many surplus workers.
"As such, employment conditions, including wages, are steadily improving," the report said.
It added that while the recovery in the labour market had become more evident recently, various indicators measuring employment conditions were showing different rates of progress.
The jobs-to-applicants ratio, which measures the number of job seekers against job openings, was improving relatively steadily but the overall unemployment rate was still at a high level, it said.
Overtime and new job openings have risen considerably but the recovery in the number of employed was only gradual.
The report attributed some of the discrepancies in the indicators to a growing mismatch between employers' needs and the type of job people want to do, particularly among young people.
It also said that firms were more likely to use overtime as a method of increasing output rather than taking on the permanent cost of hiring new employees.

Japan's unemployment rate was unchanged at 3.3 percent in February from a month earlier, a level low compared with other nations, but high for a country used to levels of less than three percent for most of the post-war era.
The jobs-to-applicants ratio fell to 0.73 in February from 0.76 percent a month earlier, the first fall since July 1995.
Economists have said, however, that the ratio's rising trend is expected to continue.
